display.purpose: Page-level titles. One per page at most.

title.purpose: Subsection headings inside a card or section.

body.purpose: All interface prose. The default size.

label.purpose: Form labels, toolbar labels, chip text, row counts.

group-label.purpose: Sidebar section headings only: 11px, 600, uppercase, wide tracking.

data.purpose: Machine-authored text only: log bodies, timestamps, ids, attribute pairs. Geist Mono, tabular-nums.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, dropdowns, popovers, sheets — elements that genuinely float.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus-visible on every interactive element, paired with a border shift to --ring. Neutral, never a hue.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for every state transition.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Colour and shadow transitions on buttons, chips, rows, inputs.

motion.name: tail-pulse
motion.purpose: The live-tail indicator while tailing — the only continuous motion in the product.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The default action. Filled with ink, never with an accent hue.

components.name: Search Input

components.css: .ds-input-wrap { position:relative; display:block; width:100%; max-width:360px; } .ds-input-icon { position:absolute; top:50%; left:12px; transform:translateY(-50%); color:var(--muted-foreground, hsl(225 9% 46%)); pointer-events:none; } .ds-input-search { width:100%; height:40px; padding:4px 12px 4px 36px; border:1px solid var(--input, hsl(225 13% 82%)); border-radius:6px; background:transparent; color:var(--foreground, hsl(225 18% 12%)); font-family:Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size:.875rem; outline:none; transition:border-color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-input-search::placeholder { color:var(--muted-foreground, hsl(225 9% 46%)); } .ds-input-search:focus-visible { border-color:var(--ring, hsl(225 12% 55%)); box-shadow:0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, hsl(225 12% 55%)) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Severity Chip
components.description: The six-level filter row. State is carried by fill, weight and dot opacity together — never by colour alone.
components.css: .ds-sev-row { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:center; gap:6px; } .ds-sev { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; padding:4px 10px; border:1px solid var(--border, hsl(225 14% 89%)); border-radius:9999px; background:var(--background, hsl(225 20% 97%)); color:var(--muted-foreground, hsl(225 9% 46%)); font-family:Geist, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size:.75rem; font-weight:500; text-transform:capitalize; cursor:pointer; outline:none; transition:color 150ms, border-color 150ms, background 150ms; } .ds-sev .ds-dot { width:8px; height:8px; border-radius:9999px; opacity:.4; transition:opacity 150ms; } .ds-sev:hover { color:var(--foreground, hsl(225 18% 12%)); } .ds-sev:focus-visible { box-shadow:0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, hsl(225 12% 55%)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-sev.is-active { background:var(--secondary, hsl(225 14% 93%)); color:var(--secondary-foreground, hsl(225 18% 18%)); font-weight:600; } .ds-sev.is-active .ds-dot { opacity:1; }

components.name: Log Entry Row
components.description: The signature component. Fixed columns, a 1px severity hairline on the left edge, and a resting tint on the levels that mean something broke.
components.css: .ds-log { width:100%; } .ds-log-row { display:flex; width:100%; align-items:flex-start; gap:12px; padding:6px 12px; border:none; border-bottom:1px solid var(--border, hsl(225 14% 89%)); border-left:1px solid var(--severity-info, hsl(212 82% 42%)); background:transparent; color:var(--foreground, hsl(225 18% 12%)); font-family:'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size:.75rem; line-height:1rem; text-align:left; cursor:pointer; transition:background 150ms; } .ds-log-row.is-error { border-left-color:var(--severity-error, hsl(2 74% 47%)); background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--severity-error, hsl(2 74% 47%)) 6%, transparent); } .ds-log-row:hover { background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent, hsl(225 16% 94%)) 50%, transparent); } .ds-log-time { flex-shrink:0; color:var(--muted-foreground, hsl(225 9% 46%)); font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; } .ds-log-sev { display:inline-flex; flex-shrink:0; align-items:center; gap:6px; width:64px; font-weight:600; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-log-sev .ds-dot { width:8px; height:8px; flex-shrink:0; border-radius:9999px; } .ds-log-svc { flex-shrink:0; width:160px; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap; color:var(--muted-foreground, hsl(225 9% 46%)); } .ds-log-body { flex:1 1 0%; min-width:0; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap; }

narrative.overview:
Bilis has exactly one idea about colour: it belongs to data, and the interface around the data does not get any. Every surface, border, button, focus ring, icon, nav item and piece of type is cut from a single neutral ladder. Only two families carry hue, and both are data — the six severity levels and the five chart series.

The reason is the job. Somebody sits in front of a log stream at two in the morning scanning thousands of monospace lines for the one that explains the outage. Anything chromatic in that field is a claim on attention. Strip the interface to grey and the ramp becomes the only signal in the room.

The neutrals are not dead grey. They all carry the same faint cool cast — hue 225 at 8-20% saturation — so they read as one material rather than a pile of unrelated greys, without ever reading as blue. Dark is the designed-for mode; light is authored properly, not derived.
keyCharacteristics: Colour belongs to data. The chrome is built from one achromatic ladder; the severity ramp and the chart series are the only things with hue, and both come from the mark's tail.
The primary action is filled with ink, never with an accent hue.
Cool-cast neutrals (hue 225) so greys read as one material, never as blue.
Geist for what the interface says, Geist Mono for what a machine wrote.
Flat at rest — depth is a response to state, never a resting property.
Dark-first: the mode this product is actually read in.
Every reusable component appears in /styleguide. A component that isn't there isn't done.

rules.name: The Chrome Is Achromatic Rule
rules.body: Colour belongs to data; chrome never gets any. Surfaces, borders, buttons, focus rings, nav, icons and type are built entirely from the neutral ladder. Destructive is the one stated exception, and it warns about an action rather than decorating the interface.

rules.name: The Data Gets Colour Rule
rules.body: Two families are allowed hue, because both are data: the severity ramp, and the five categorical chart series. Both are drawn from the mark's tail — gold, teal, navy, crimson — and both are ordered so adjacent members separate by hue rather than by saturation.

rules.name: The Reserved Ramp Rule
rules.body: The six severity values mean severity and nothing else. A severity chart reads --severity-* directly rather than approximating it from the chart palette.

rules.name: The One Cast Rule
rules.body: Every neutral carries hue 225 at 8-20% saturation. A dead 0%-saturation grey, or a neutral mixed from another hue, breaks the material.

rules.name: The Twice-Tuned Rule
rules.body: Every value that appears in both modes is authored twice. Never derive a dark value by fading or lightening its light counterpart.

rules.name: The Monospace Boundary Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks machine-authored text. Log bodies, timestamps, ids and attribute pairs are Geist Mono; every label about them drops back to Geist.

rules.name: The 14/12 Rule
rules.body: Interface copy is 14px and support copy is 12px. There is no 16px body and no 13px anything.

rules.name: The Tabular Timestamp Rule
rules.body: Any column of digits a reader scans vertically is tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Surface Declaration Rule
rules.body: A rounded-lg border alone sits at page level and disappears. Anything that should read as a surface must declare bg-card.

rules.name: The Fixed Column Rule
rules.body: In the log stream every column left of the message has a fixed width. Nothing shifts between rows.

rules.name: The Shell Owns The Scroll Rule
rules.body: The document never scrolls in the app. A scroll container must have a definite-height ancestor and be a containing block, or absolutely positioned descendants escape its clip.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: If an element's state has not changed, it casts no shadow. Structure is carried by tone and hairline.

rules.name: The Hairline-Only Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px. To emphasise an element, change its fill or its tone; never thicken its stroke.

dos: Do build every non-data element from the neutral ladder — surfaces, borders, buttons, focus rings, icons, type.
Do give every panel that should read as a surface bg-card.
Do reference semantic tokens rather than raw values.
Do author every value twice — a hand-tuned light value and a hand-tuned dark value.
Do pair severity colour with the dot and the uppercase label. Colour never carries severity alone.
Do use tabular-nums on any column of digits scanned vertically.
Do keep Geist Mono for machine-authored text and Geist for everything the interface says about it.
Do add every new reusable component to /styleguide in the same change.
Do keep borders at 1px and create emphasis with fill or tone.
donts: Don't introduce an accent colour, a brand hue, a coloured primary button, or a coloured link. Colour is for data.
Don't borrow a severity colour for anything that isn't log severity.
Don't use a dead 0%-saturation grey or a neutral mixed from another hue — every neutral is hue 225.
Don't derive a dark-mode value by fading or lightening its light counterpart.
Don't put a resting shadow on a surface.
Don't let column widths vary between log rows.
Don't introduce a third interface type size. 14px body and 12px support carry the product.
Don't hardcode a chart colour or import from 'echarts' — go through lib/echarts.ts and useChartTokens().
Don't let the document scroll in the app shell; the content column owns the scroll.
